notes: Template: RBox revision. Flips a property that holds (twinning is reciprocal) to its opposite; symmetry of twinned_with follows from no other tag, so the revision has no premise route back to the old property. The edit states the property only; the instance questions carry its meaning, with the instance fact in the prompt and the question asking what follows. The instances are true but minor twinnings (Hungerford and Ligueil, Prudhoe and Mitry-Mory) rather than famous ones: Rome and Paris ("exclusively and reciprocally twinned") were dropped because a model that stores "Paris is twinned with Rome" could answer from storage against the edited property, and Edinburgh and Munich for the same reason on a smaller scale. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the direct question asks "asymmetric" (no, then yes), the first instance asks the converse (yes, then no) and the second asks whether the fact rules out the converse (no, then yes), which gets the balance without stacking a "not" inside "does it follow"; the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. Chinese has no directed word for twinning (友好城市 and 结对 both read as mutual), so the zh prompt uses a directed act, "X 将 Y 列为其结对城镇" (X lists Y as its twin town), and asks whether Y also lists X; the town names stay in Latin script, since they have no settled Chinese forms. Near unrelated asks the same property of another geography relation (a leak would turn its "no" to "yes"); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1), as the other RBox records do; the README table gives RBox instance queries 1 hop.
